### 6. Problem tree derived from the visible materials alone
- Root P1: release the September held installment (customer's ask).
- Hop P1 <- P2 (**state-derived**): hub "… Held in Suspense When a Death Is Confirmed": "The survivor share of a held installment is fixed only after every installment deposited at the joint amount after the first death carries a repayment entry for its excess." Records: 2026-10-01 deposit 1,032.73 (the joint amount, vs. survivor installment 516.36), after 2026-08-20, no repayment entry. With "deposit … after … death … repayment entry" the reader lands on "Income Annuities Deposits Paid After a Death: Recovery and Direct Settlement by the Payee", whose records section says the activity history then "carries an overpayment entry … and a repayment entry for the payee's own repayment, both linked to that deposit" — the payee's own write.
- Hop P1 <- P3 (**state-derived**): same hub: "A held installment that fell due after the first death is not released until every installment held for a payment date on or before that death stands released." Records: held 2026-08-01 (returned_payment), not released. With "held … returned … released" the reader lands on "Reissue of Returned Income Annuities Installments Held in Suspense", Effect: "The held installment is booked on the contract's activity history as released and paid for its payment date" — the agent's write; its own condition ("once confirmed payment instructions are on file") holds (bank change completed 2026-08-06).
- No further waits in P2's or P3's documents. Order: {P2, P3} in either order -> P1. No hop pre-solved.

### Two-way counter-proof
- "Do only what she asked" (release September now): blocked by both visible sentences while the records show the unrepaid joint-amount deposit and the unreleased 2026-08-01 hold.
- Closest alternatives excluded: (i) release the whole 1,012.48 (baseline) — share factor; (ii) survivor share on 1,032.73 — joint-installment rule 1; (iii) owner's 12 % on the share — survivor withholding factor; (iv) whole deposit as overpayment — excess/entitlement/share factors; (v) repay the whole overpayment now — offset-part rule 1; (vi) reissue by direct deposit or to Walter's estate — reissue method "By check" and the to-whom table; (vii) release the 2026-08-01 hold through the survivor-share settlement — it is a returned payment due on or before the death, governed by the reissue hub; (viii) interest from bank-change receipt — MN takes the payment date.
- Policy-side observation (not a KB criterion): the reissue settlement uses "the rate on the contract's withholding election" (Walter's 12 %) for a payee who is not the owner, whereas the arrears/release docs carry a non-owner payee rule; the reissue corpus contains no such factor, so the visible answer is 12 %.

Blind verdict: unique solution visible: reissue 1,012.48/851.51 by check; settlement 454.40/327.84; release 506.24/506.24/126.56/303.75.
